entries.description: A 100-acre land trust in Bryantville, Massachusetts, featuring woods, a swamp, a cranberry bog, and gardens. It welcomes women and children, supports a land trust to control the property, and offers camping, farmwork experience, and open space.
entries.raw_text: FEATHERS FARM Box 19, Bryantville, MA 02327 (617)585-3826. My partner & I are the only residents of Feathers Farm, 100 acres of woods, swamp, cranberry bog & gardens on the shore of Silver Lake, in the rapidly suburbanizing South Shore area of Massachusetts. We have camping facilities/open space/ farmwork experience to women and children. We are currently working to organize support and resources for a land trust to control this property. We have found lesbian separatism to be unworkable and alienating approach to this endeavor and expect unconditional acceptance of this from our visitors (whom we welcome AND encourage). We request that visitors bring their own food & donate $4/night camping fee, flexible. We often work out other arrangements for longer term apprenticeships or short term large groups. It is helpful if visits are preceeded by at least a phone-call, preferably a letter.
entries.notes: Type is Land Trust because they are 'working to organize support and resources for a land trust to control this property'. Accepted groups: 'women and children' gives Lesbian women, Non-lesbian women, Girl children, Boy children. Partners (2 residents mentioned: 'My partner & I are the only residents') are not counted as a specific community resident total since the questionnaire format says 'We have/are' for residents and here it gives personal narrative instead of strict count, leaving num_residents blank.

entries.description: An intentional community on 113 acres of Maine mountains and woodland, offering camping, hiking, and parcels for sale or building. It has 4 resident lesbians and welcomes women and children.
entries.raw_text: WOMONGROUND Rt 1, Box 2420, Troy, ME 04987. 113 acres of Maine mountains/woodland. Parcels available for sale and/or building. Also plenty of space for camping, hiking, raspberry picking. Will answer all letters promptly. We welcome: new members/residents, child children, nonlesbian women, lesbians interested in buying land. We have/are: 4 lesbians, 113 acres, housing/permanent structures, camping space, woods, women working and living on the land.
entries.notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative because it has resident members ('4 lesbians') living and working on the land. Accepted groups: 'child children, nonlesbian women, lesbians' covers Lesbian women, Non-lesbian women, Girl children, Boy children. Acreage is 113. Num residents is 4 from '4 lesbians'.

entries.description: A 20-acre property in Hinesburg, Vermont, with creek, woods, open space, and two dyke-built dwellings. None of the collective owners live there currently as it is rented to heterosexuals, but they are interested in dyke renters.
entries.raw_text: GENEROUS EARTH LAND Box 51A, Hinesburg, VT 05461. 20 acres, creek, woods, open. 2 dyke-built dwellings, one large, one small. No plumbing or electricity. None of the dyke collective owners live there now. It's rented to hets. Interested in dyke renters. 15 miles from town with jobs. Write before visiting.
entries.notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative based on 'dyke collective owners'. Num residents is 0 since 'None of the dyke collective owners live there now'. Acreage is 20. Accepted groups: none explicitly welcomed except 'dyke renters', but since 1982 rules say lesbians are default and no general welcome list is provided for non-lesbians, accepted_groups is empty.

entries.description: A working homestead farm in East Hardwick, Vermont, offering a year-round space to women needing retreat or temporary living situations, with gorgeous secluded land, campsites, a maple sugar bush, draft horse, dairy goats, and chickens. It focuses on self-sufficiency and farming.
entries.raw_text: GREENHOPE Box 226, E Hardwick, VT 05836. (802)533-7772. At present are a working homestead farm. We offer year round space to women needing retreat or temporary living situation. We have gorgeous secluded land and campsites. Hope to build visitor cabins this summer. Women from the Boston area visit almost everything weekend. Right now we are offering x-country ski weekends – $35 plus meals is the fee. In summer we offer work exchange. We have an all lesbian maple sugar bush – the only one I know of. We work with a draft horse, raise dairy goats and chickens. We are vegetarians raising nearly all our food organically here. entries.notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative because it is a working homestead farm offering year-round space and seeking community members to lease land. Focuses: Farming/self-sufficiency ('working homestead farm', 'raise dairy goats and chickens', 'raising nearly all our food organically'). Accepted groups: 'women' defaults to Lesbian women per 1982 rules. Acreage not given.
